title: [GMCP 203.017.02] Production path: Complete MCP client and host
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-017-02. Implement the canonical state, types, and primary production path. Replace stubs, demo-only paths, duplicated semantics, and implicit ambient state; preserve compatible behavior through explicit adapters; and make the new path reachable from the shipped GMCP runtime. Vector outcome: GMCP is a full host, not only a tool caller: one API and CLI can connect to any supported server, discover capabilities, call tools, read and subscribe to resources, get prompts and completions, handle MRTR callbacks, tasks, Apps, authorization, notifications, progress and cancellation. Multiple servers operate concurrently with isolated identities, policies and state, and every callback surface is exercised against real reference servers. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
limitations: Production stage (`GMCP-203-017-02`) ships the canonical multi-server `susi_wire_client::host::McpHost` and extended `susi_wire_client::mcp::Session` (`HOST-001..HOST-018`), `susi_tools::spawn_authorized_stdio_peer` (`CLAIM-04`), and unified `susi mcp` CLI subcommands (`discover`, `resources`, `read [--app]`, `prompts`, `prompt`, `complete`, `task`); integration, adversarial, interop, operations, and `.M` mastery ship across `T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-116..120`.

Per `docs/gmcp/contract-203-017.md` and zero-UI plan A9, Core ships headless MCP host protocol plumbing and `ui://` metadata inspection while interactive Apps rendering lives in Susi Commercial Apps, and `.agents/gmcp/evidence/VC-203-017.jsonl` plus `.agents/roadmap-verdicts/VC-203-017.json` remain strictly absent until `T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-120` (`.M` Mastery).

reuse.why: Extended `susi-wire-client` (`Session` + `host::McpHost`), `susi_tools::mcp_budget::spawn_authorized_stdio_peer`, and `susi mcp` CLI definitions/handlers on top of existing thin-client framing, `MacPolicy` transport authorization, and `PersistedTaskHandleStore` without adding workspace or third-party dependencies.
